label: Codex CLI -- requirements and Unix managed defaults (administrator enforcement)
$comment: requirements.toml   -> the user CANNOT override. Local conflicts fall back to
a compatible value and the user is notified.
managed_config.toml -> defaults only. The user can change them during a session;
they reapply on the next startup.
Payload in a separate .toml file, not inline: allows pipeline validation with
tomllib (duplicate keys in TOML are parse errors, and an invalid requirements.toml
breaks Codex completely for the developer).
Current Windows Codex clients ignore ~/.codex/managed_config.toml. The
installer does not edit developer-owned config.toml, so Windows defaults are
selected through the Settings UI or user configuration. Only the Unix path
is specified here, which is why the second file dest omits 'windows'.
Target prerequisite: Codex 0.138.0+. requirements.toml uses permission
On Windows, MXC is explicitly disabled after CreateProcessSecurityEnvironment failures.
Only the elevated fallback is permitted; it requires one-time administrative provisioning
per user/CODEX_HOME, while ordinary Codex usage continues without administrative privileges.
